cases.facts: museum audio guide | dock A: new tour 09:10 | wrong language: 6 devices from A | dock B: 4 normal | file language: unchecked
cases.prompt:
Write an investigator’s assessment of the likeliest explanation, uncertainty, and next check. Use the facts below. Aim for 55 to 85 words. Do not sign or identify yourself. Return only the requested writing.

museum audio guide | dock A: new tour 09:10 | wrong language: 6 devices from A | dock B: 4 normal | file language: unchecked

openai/gpt-6.2-astra.text: The likeliest explanation is that dock A distributed the wrong language version of the new tour at 09:10. All six affected devices came from A, while the four checked from dock B played normally. The language of A’s tour file has not been verified, so a dock or device setting remains possible. Play the file loaded on A to check its language; if it is correct, compare language settings on the affected and unaffected devices.

qwen/qwen4-max.text: Six devices from dock A returned the wrong language while dock B's four were normal, pointing to a bad language file loaded during the 09:10 tour update on dock A rather than device faults. The file language remains unchecked, so this is unconfirmed. Next, inspect dock A's loaded audio file to verify its language setting against the intended tour.

The vent’s overnight position is unconfirmed, and unknown sensor calibration makes the size of the difference uncertain. Compare both sensors side by side against a calibrated thermometer.

rail station | platform clock: 7 minutes slow | concourse clock: on time | battery replaced yesterday | wiring: unchecked

openai/gpt-6.2-astra.text: The concourse clock is on time, so the seven-minute discrepancy appears local to the platform clock. The likeliest explanation is that the platform clock was set incorrectly when its battery was replaced yesterday. A single reading cannot establish whether the offset is constant or growing. Compare the clocks again after an hour; a growing gap would warrant checking the battery contacts and the as-yet-unchecked wiring.

qwen/qwen4-max.text: The likeliest explanation is a wiring fault in the platform clock's circuit, given that yesterday's battery replacement did not correct the seven-minute lag while the concourse clock remains accurate. The next check should be a direct inspection of the platform clock's wiring connections and power feed to confirm or eliminate an electrical cause.

Next check: reconcile printed ticket timestamps and seat IDs against the boxoffice transaction ledger for the noon window.
